abstract: Fitting a large model in an older GPU's memory does not ensure fast decoding. We adapted exllamav3's kernels to run the original Qwen3.8-27B weights at 2 bits per weight on a stock 11 GiB RTX 2080 Ti, a 2018 consumer card. Pre-registered rotated rounds compared the patched and stock engines on three prompts. The patched engine decoded 47.53 tokens/s undrafted, 1.88 times stock, and 71.61 with the model's multi-token-prediction (MTP) head, 1.54 times stock; a second session matched within 1%. Most of the undrafted gain comes from an int8 path fitted to Turing's shared memory with unfused projections. Split-K verification and tensor-core attention support drafting and filled contexts. The patches changed no GSM8K outcome in the registered MTP check. On 500 GSM8K and 500 MMLU items, the stock engine's EXL3 weights scored 97.6% and 86.6%; differences from llama.cpp's 2-bit GGUFs were unresolved after adjustment. An 8-bit key-value cache held 72K tokens, and the tensor-core kernel retained the reference kernel's retrieval accuracy at 64K. These measurements show how kernels adapted to an older card recover decode speed after low-bit weights make the model fit. They cover our fastest measured configuration of the original weights on one card and three prompts, not the fastest model on the card; dated comparisons and detailed limits are in the appendix.
